He made the problem smaller. Legal-sized.

He called counsel.

"Counsel," he said when she answered, "they filed an emergency family-court petition and leaked fake medical records."

There was a pause. Not shock—calculation.

"They're escalating into the 'protection' frame," counsel said. "Understood."

Sandi leaned closer.

Counsel continued, "Do not respond publicly. Do not deny. Do not explain."

Sandi's eyes narrowed. "But people will believe it."

Counsel's voice stayed calm. "We're not fighting belief. We're fighting process."

One said, "What's the move?"

Counsel answered, crisp as a scalpel:

"We file to remove it to federal jurisdiction if possible. We file an emergency motion for protective order. We demand provenance of the leak. We request Executive Security logs again. And Sandi gets separate counsel on record today."

Sandi swallowed. "So I'm not just 'his partner.' I'm my own witness."

"Yes," counsel said. "That's the point."

One's throat tightened. "And the fake medical record?"

Counsel's tone sharpened slightly.

"We treat it as retaliation and defamation connected to witness intimidation. We don't argue about whether it's 'true.' We demand the source. We demand chain-of-custody. We force the lie to pick a body."

Sandi let out a breath. Almost a laugh. Almost a sob.

One looked at her.

"You okay?" he asked softly.

Sandi's eyes glistened, but her voice held.

"I'm… angry," she said. "Because it's clever."

One nodded once. "That's why we don't improvise. We document."

Sandi stared at the petition again.

"They're using the baby," she said quietly. "Even without seeing the baby."

One closed his eyes for a beat. That same line, now true twice.

He opened them and looked at her like a vow.

"They're not getting our child," he said. "And they're not turning you into a diagnosis."

Sandi's face tightened. "What if the only way to stop it is to tell the world everything?"

There it was.

The trap.

If they go loud, they feed the machine.
If they go quiet, the lie spreads.

One sat down slowly, hands flat on the table.

His voice came out warm, but tired.

"This is the part where truth and privacy start fighting each other," he said.

Sandi watched him. "And?"

One looked at the baby monitor—tiny green lights, steady, innocent.

And the dagger point finally slipped out, barely louder than a whisper:

"I hate that my truth became a weapon they can swing at you."

Sandi reached across the table and squeezed his hand.

"Don't turn this into guilt," she said gently. "Turn it into craft."

One nodded.

He opened a new document.

Not a press statement.

A formal submission.

Title:

SUPPLEMENTAL DECLARATION: RETALIATORY ACTIONS FOLLOWING TESTIMONY

And he began to write the only kind of words Carmichael couldn't eat:

dates, exhibits, demands, proof.

Outside, the internet roared.

Inside, they stayed boring on purpose.

Because boring is how you win in court.

And court is where spectacle goes to die.

entries.title: Scene: The Warm Rescue
entries.summary: Carmichael sends velvet, not soldiers — an offer of rescue dressed as mercy. Sandi answers the door alone.
entries.body:
Scene: The Warm Rescue

They didn’t send soldiers.

They sent velvet.

It came two days after the hearing, timed perfectly—after the smear had soaked in, after the “concern” headlines had done their quiet work, after the public had been taught what to feel before they knew what was true.

Sandi was alone when it arrived.

Not truly alone—there were layers of protection around the apartment, eyes and protocols and counsel on speed dial—but alone in the only way that matters: alone in the moment where a decision is offered as mercy.

The knock was soft. Respectful. The kind of knock that pretends it has no right to be there.

Sandi looked through the peephole.

A woman stood in the hallway in a neutral coat, no jewelry, no visible weapon. She held a slim folder and a second envelope sealed with a familiar crest—old power, old money, old family.

Sandi’s chest tightened, not with fear but with recognition.

This is how Carmichael spoke when he wanted to own your emotions.

Sandi didn’t open the door. She spoke through it.

“Who are you?”

The woman didn’t flinch. “My name is Elaine Porter. I’m authorized counsel for the Office of Executive Security.”

Sandi almost laughed. Executive Security. A name that could mean anything.

“What do you want?” Sandi asked.

Elaine lifted the sealed envelope slightly, so it could be seen through the glass.

“A private message,” she said. “From your father.”

Sandi’s jaw tightened at the word father. Not because she missed him. Because the word still had hooks.

“I’m not taking anything,” Sandi said.

Elaine nodded like she expected that. Like she’d been trained for it.

“I understand,” Elaine said gently. “I’m not here to force you. I’m here to offer you… a clean exit.”

Sandi’s stomach turned.

“Exit from what?” she asked.

Elaine’s voice stayed soft—soft like a blanket, soft like a trap.

“From the noise,” she said. “From the danger. From the spectacle that’s forming around you.”

Sandi didn’t answer.

Elaine continued, careful, as if speaking to someone in grief.

“You have a child,” Elaine said. “Whether or not the public can prove it, the state has a duty to ensure safety. That duty can become… complicated.”

Sandi felt heat rise in her throat.

“So this is a threat,” she said.

Elaine shook her head quickly, almost offended. “No. It’s protection.”

Protection. The sweetest word power uses.

“I’m not alone,” Sandi said.

“I know,” Elaine replied, and the way she said it was a reminder: we see you.

Sandi’s fingers tightened around the edge of the door.

Elaine’s voice dropped lower, intimate, like confession.

“Your father is willing to let you disappear,” she said. “For real. Not rumors. Not safe houses. A new identity. New documentation. A protected lane. Medical access. Legal insulation.”

Sandi closed her eyes for a moment, because the offer was designed to sound like relief.

Elaine added the blade:

“For you and the baby.”

Sandi opened her eyes again. “And One?”

Elaine hesitated. Just a fraction. That fraction was the truth.

“Your father can’t extend the same protections to him,” Elaine said. “He’s become… a public destabilization vector.”

Sandi let out a slow breath. “Say it plainly.”

Elaine met the peephole like she could see Sandi through it.

“He has to be separated from you,” Elaine said. “For this to work.”

There it was.

Not a kidnapping. Not a prison.

A rescue that required betrayal.

Sandi’s voice went cold. “You want me to renounce him.”

Elaine didn’t say yes. She didn’t have to. She offered language instead.

“A statement,” Elaine said. “Simple. You can call it mental health concerns. You can call it manipulation. You can call it coercive control. Whatever framing helps you move on.”

Sandi’s hands shook now—not because she believed it, but because she understood how effective it would be.

They weren’t trying to destroy One through law.

They were trying to destroy him through love.

“Tell my father,” Sandi said quietly, “that I’m not doing this.”

Elaine stayed gentle. “You don’t have to decide right now.”

“I just did,” Sandi replied.

Elaine’s voice softened further, as if Sandi were being unreasonable.

“Ms. Carmichael,” she said, using the old name like a key, “this is a mercy. The storm that’s coming—”

“Don’t,” Sandi said, and her voice cracked on the word. Not from weakness. From anger that still had grief inside it.

Elaine paused.

Then she did what good operatives do: she shifted the frame.

“This isn’t about him,” Elaine said. “This is about your child.”

Sandi went very still. That was the point.

Elaine continued, almost whispering now, as if offering comfort.

“Children don’t choose their parents,” she said. “But mothers choose safety.”

Sandi’s throat tightened. Her eyes burned.

And for one second, the thought flashed through her like lightning:

If I do this, the baby is safe.

Then another thought followed, quieter but stronger:

Safe inside whose story?

Sandi leaned her forehead against the door.

“You’re good,” she said softly. “I’ll give you that.”

Elaine didn’t reply.

Sandi straightened, wiped her face once, and spoke clearly, like a woman writing her own name into the record.

“I’m not handing my child to a man who wants to turn the child into a symbol,” she said. “And I’m not saving myself by destroying someone else.”

Elaine’s voice sharpened a hair. “You’re choosing him over your child?”

Sandi’s heart lurched. That question was poison.

She answered anyway—slow, controlled.

“No,” she said. “I’m choosing my child over your narrative.”

Silence.

Elaine exhaled once, as if disappointed.

“I’ll leave the envelope,” she said. “You can read it when you’re calm.”

Sandi didn’t move.

A soft sound behind her—floorboard, a shift—One coming from the other room. He’d been there the whole time, just out of sight, letting Sandi have the moment without hovering.

Elaine’s voice, still outside the door, became faintly satisfied.

“He heard that?” she asked.

Sandi didn’t answer.

Elaine continued, sweet as a lullaby:

“Because if he loves you,” she said, “he’ll let you go.”

And then she walked away, footsteps quiet, professional, unhurried.

Sandi stood frozen for a moment, fighting the urge to collapse.

One stepped into the hallway behind her.

He didn’t touch her right away.

He looked at the door like it had teeth.

Sandi turned to him. Her eyes were wet but steady.

“They want me to leave you,” she said.

One’s face tightened—anger, pain, recognition.

And then, the dagger point:

His voice came out raw, almost broken.

“This is what I got you into.”

Sandi opened her mouth to argue.

One didn’t let her.

“I can take the smear,” he said. “I can take the threats. I can take their little lawsuits and their little scripts.”

His hands trembled now. Not fear—rage restrained.

“But you shouldn’t have to carry this,” he whispered. “You shouldn’t have to be used as a weapon against me.”

Sandi stepped closer.

“One—”

He shook his head, eyes shining.

“If you get hurt because of me,” he said, voice collapsing into honesty, “I’ll never forgive myself… even if I’m right.”

The room went quiet.

Sandi reached up and held his face between her hands, forcing him to look at her.

“Listen to me,” she said, gentle but firm. “Don’t steal my choice.”

One swallowed hard.

Sandi’s voice stayed warm.

“I’m not here because it’s safe,” she said. “I’m here because it’s true.”

One closed his eyes for a second, like the words were both a wound and medicine.

Sandi pulled him in, forehead to forehead.

“And if you ever think you have to let me go to prove you love me,” she whispered, “remember this: that’s their logic. Not ours.”

One exhaled, shaky.

He looked at the table where the envelope had been slid under the door—still untouched, still sealed, still trying to write their story for them.

One walked over and picked it up.

He didn’t open it.

He held it like evidence.

Then he did the most “One” thing possible:

He wrote on the front, in black pen, neat and calm:

RECEIVED. REFUSED. ENTERED INTO THE RECORD.

He set it down.

And for a moment, the machine had nothing to feed on.

Just two people, holding the line.

⸻

entries.title: Warm Scene Version — What Is This Story?
entries.summary: A short sample scene used as a demonstration: One in a federal building, offered a loyalty agreement by Carmichael's orbit, refusing to sign.
entries.body:
Here’s a warm scene-version you can drop straight into chat — it answers “what’s the story?” by showing it.

⸻

One’s sitting in a windowless office in a federal building that smells like old carpet and burnt coffee. Not a glamorous place. Not a heroic place. Just fluorescent light and paper and the quiet hum of a machine that never sleeps.

Across the table is a senior staffer from President Carmichael’s orbit—polite voice, cold eyes—sliding a folder toward him like it’s a courtesy.

“Sign this. You’ll be protected. You’ll have access. You’ll be useful.”

One doesn’t open it right away. He already knows what it is: a loyalty agreement dressed up as “national stability.” A clean little document that turns conscience into compliance.

In the hallway outside, a TV is playing the President’s speech on loop. The crowd is cheering. The words are warm. The intent underneath them isn’t.

One finally opens the folder. The language is smooth. Legal. Almost gentle. It doesn’t say “purge,” it says “reform.” It doesn’t say “silence,” it says “unify.” It doesn’t say “enemy,” it says “threat.”

He looks up. “And if I don’t sign?”

The staffer smiles like this is all very reasonable. “Then you’ll be… difficult. And difficult people don’t last long in this city.”

That’s when One understands what his job really is. Not to win. Not to overthrow. Just to create friction—paper trails, audits, procedural delays, coalition pressure—anything that buys time and forces truth into daylight.

Later that night, Sandi finds him on the steps outside, coat pulled tight, eyes tired in the way only someone raised near power can be tired.

“You can’t fight him,” she says softly. Not as a warning. As a confession.

One doesn’t argue. He just says, “I’m not trying to destroy him. I’m trying to stop the part of him that doesn’t care who gets crushed.”

She sits beside him, close enough to feel the heat of his breath in the cold.

“And what does that make you?” she asks.

One watches the lights in the windows above them—hundreds of rooms full of people choosing comfort over conflict.

“It makes me a witness,” he says. “And if I can… a lock on the door.”

And somewhere upstairs, Carmichael is still speaking into the cameras, smiling like a savior—while the country slowly learns the difference between comfort and conscience.

⸻

entries.title: A Prophet Ain't Nothing but a Sandwich
entries.summary: A performable satirical play with Off-Broadway energy, hip-hop chorus, and mythic comedy. Part of the Pandemic Papers.
entries.body:
Absolutely. I kept the off-Broadway chaos, the hip-hop chorus energy, and the mythic satire, but I made it performable: clearer voices, cleaner stage directions, tighter rhythm, and I removed the hard racial slurs (you don’t need them to get the punch). Part of "the pandemic papers meaning prophetic stories published during the Pandemic.

⸻

A Prophet Ain’t Nothing but a Sandwich

First Notes (❤️)

ACT I

PROLOGUE — Invocation

(A bare stage. A neon sign flickers: EINSTEIN SQUARE. Distant sirens. A subway rumble under everything.)

MUSES (spoken-sung, overlapping)
As rappers and muses—
Alpha is plus, Beta is minus.
Muses who dwell in Heaven, begin the tale!
Once more!
Of the one who turned water into wine,
and a fish into a banquet—
of Jesus of Nazareth…
and of the one who came after,
and lost his senses.

⸻

SCENE 1 — Einstein Square

(The CHORUS pours in like a living crowd. They’re ring-bells, holding vape pens, wearing winter coats over glitter. Light beams cut through haze like stained glass.)

CHORUS (chanting)
The crowds gather round in Einstein Square—
so many faces—
light in the air—
it hits the eyes, it wakes the senses.

(A beat drops. The CHORUS shifts into a call-and-response.)

CHORUS
Everyone is everyone!
EVERYONE IS EVERYONE!
Everyone is everyone!
EVERYONE IS EVERYONE!

(An OLD MESSENGER steps forward — half prophet, half subway philosopher.)

OLD MESSENGER
He who came before the Baptist—
in that old-man slant—
says the bell has rung again.
He who you wait for
has left Heaven
and missed his stop.

CHORUS (explodes)
WAIT UP!

(UNCLE BERNIE storms in, confused, furious, holding a deli sandwich like evidence.)

UNCLE BERNIE
Uncle Bernie—what the hell is going on?

(VILLAGE PEOPLE enter ringing bells and vaping like it’s sacred incense.)

VILLAGE PEOPLE (wild, joyous)
Everyone is everyone!
Everyone is everyone!

CHORUS (prophetic hype)
Children of war!
Sons of prophets!
Arrival of the saint!
Burning of the sand!
These children are no longer children!
If He has returned—
let Him show his face in Times Square!
You know what we mean.

UNCLE BERNIE
Hold up—HOLD UP.

(The DIRECTOR appears at the edge of the stage with a clipboard. Pensive. Like this show is happening to them.)

DIRECTOR (low)
Places.

⸻

SCENE 2 — The City as Fever Dream

(LIGHTS: Red/Green. Crosswalk strobes. Manhattan winter. Everything shiny and too expensive. A quick montage of projections: caviar, Fabergé eggs, Broadway marquees, a stock ticker bleeding red.)

ENSEMBLE / CHORUS (layered, rhythmic)
Red light. Green light. Streets.
Manhattan in winter—
caviar dreams, cracked concrete.
Police and synchronicity—
Broadway on fire.
Ground zero—biohazard.
Wall Street in tatters.

(A loudspeaker VOICE interrupts like a public-service announcement from hell.)

LOUDSPEAKER VOICE
Beta males and fem-bots. Lawyers in therapy.
Please listen for instructions.

CHORUS (snaps back, dancing)
Psychedelic tripping—on the bus, on the train,
all the way up to Harlem—
forget that—
the D line, baby. Capisce?

(TRAFFIC COPS, LIEUTENANTS, “SONS OF SAM,” disco ghosts, sheriffs, burglars, Al Capone, and Santa Clauses all cross the stage in choreographed gridlock.)

CHORUS
Left or right—national divide.
Giants stadium, subway series—
last one out, flush the toilet, please!
Viruses and bacteria—children of Earth, listen—
that smoke burns lungs like kryptonite.

UNCLE BERNIE (deadpan)
Are you done yet?

CHORUS
HELL NO!

CHORUS (shouting over itself)
Democracy is on acid!
Love, drugs, rock and roll!
Cartels and cabals!
Democracy on fire!

Democrat versus Republican—
rise of hip-hop—
conservative versus liberal—
socialists, Bolsheviks—
black, white—
Jesus Christ Superstar!

(BACKUP SINGER CHRISSY steps out with a mic. She sings one line like a heavenly interruption.)

CHRISSY (singing)
(soft, haunting)
Red light… green light… streets…

(Beat stops.)

DIRECTOR (firm)
Pause.
Slow your flow.
Breathe. Breathe. Breathe.

(Distant music. A French crooner voice. AZNAVOUR’s “Cabotin” drifts in like an old memory.)

ORCHESTRA (offstage, chaos-jazz)
(blazing, uncontrolled)

CHORUS (dazzled, sarcastic)
Songs and lyrics. Choruses and stages.
Costumes, jewels, masks on faces.
Ballerinas, rappers, props, and sages—

(THE PHANTOM OF THE OPERA appears for one second like a hallucination.)

PHANTOM (growling, amused)
If you’re not feeling it—turn the volume down.

(The CHORUS laughs. The DIRECTOR does not.)

NARRATOR (popping in, too loud)
Pages often burn when messengers sing praises!

ENSEMBLE (snaps)
Narrator—shut up! This ain’t normal!

⸻

SCENE 3 — “Return of the Messiah?”

CHORUS (whispering, building)
Return of the Messiah?

OLD MESSENGER
No, son. Stay tuned.

(A figure enters: THE JESUS PERSON. Stylish, ambiguous. Not quite holy, not quite celebrity. The crowd can’t decide what they’re seeing.)

NARRATOR (announcing, messy)
In walks the Jesus person—pronounce it “Hey-SOOS,” Latino-style!

He looks like a rock star and a street saint
had a baby in a subway station.

(Chaos on set. Someone knocks over a prop. A smear of stage blood on the carpet.)

NARRATOR (shouting)
SLAP THAT TRUMPET!
Heaven is a place on Earth!

CHORUS (in awe, then laughter)
Sons and daughters of Heaven came through—
no IDs, no papers—
right past the wall like it was a suggestion.

Only in America!

DIRECTOR
Narrator—STOP.

CHORUS (yelling)
SECURITY!

(A BORDER AGENT storms in, hard hat, flashlight, and a portable “WALL” piece rolls in like a gag.)

BORDER AGENT
Oh please.
Another web-made miracle designed to “bring Jesus back.”
Tell the others: I’m not buying it.

(A MAN WITH A LADDER climbs up like he’s about to fix Heaven’s lighting.)

MAN WITH LADDER
Before what?
Before it’s too late?
Before the Antichrist runs this place?

BORDER AGENT
Not on my watch.
Halo, crown—don’t care.
Homeland everything—
surveillance and satellites—
welcome to Earth.

⸻

SCENE 4 — Mirror on the Wall

NARRATOR (mock-grand)
Mirror, mirror on the wall—
who’s the fairest of them all?

(GANGSTER RAPPERS and BEAUTY QUEENS flood the stage, talking trash like it’s scripture.)

RAPPER 1
OGs in the garden talking “return to Eden”—yo, stop it.

BEAUTY QUEEN
Pass Adam something sweet and watch him fall again.

RAPPER 2
Wash your mouth with cough syrup and Bible verses.

USHER / TICKET TAKER (trying to do a job)
Sir—do you have a ticket?
Or are we insinuating… trespassing?

RAPPER 1
Drake ain’t in the garden.
Didn’t come down from Toronto.
But somebody did.

(CUT.)

DIRECTOR (clapping, desperate)
Chorus—look alive!
Rap like you mean it!

CHORUS (chant, multilingual, silly-serious)
Cabeza, my people—cabeza!
This ain’t your mama’s baked beans—whatever that means!
It’s getting hot up in here—
shut up—keep moving!

⸻

SCENE 5 — Flight Plan

(The stage becomes an airplane aisle. “SOUL PLANE” energy. FLIGHT ATTENDANTS, STRIPPERS, PRIESTS, NUNS, POLE DANCERS. Everyone is airborne in the mind.)

CHORUS
Airborne gangsters and saints—
Maverick dreams—Top Gun ships—
SOS and embassies, corruption and bribery!

OFFICIAL (saluting, absurd)
Permission to speak openly!

CHORUS (shouting)
Permission to take off—
people are leaving Earth today—
every color, every kind!

OFFICIAL
Granted!

(Beat drops out. Silence. The fun drains.)

⸻

SCENE 6 — The Reveal Attempt

NARRATOR (serious, finally)
Seriously speaking—
the fun is over.

This new one is neither Jesus
nor His nemesis.

So who is he?

(A pause. The light narrows.)

NARRATOR (low)
The truth burns.
It burns.

(A “SECRETARY FOR PEACE” enters like a diplomat in a nightclub — crisp suit, glitter tie, clipboard like a weapon.)

SECRETARY FOR PEACE
Dear sirs and madams—kings and queens, princes and duchesses—
let me introduce the philosopher.

You decide who is the messenger.

Don’t be afraid of words.
Say it.
Say it like candy.

(A list of “celebrity witnesses” is projected as silhouettes — not literal names, more like archetypes: THE SINGER, THE ICON, THE COMEDIAN, THE PRINCE.)

SECRETARY FOR PEACE (repeats, ritual)
Dear sirs and madams—kings and queens, princes and duchesses—
let me introduce the philosopher.
You decide who is the messenger.

(The CHORUS murmurs: “2020… coronavirus… third planet from the sun… vaccines…”)

NARRATOR (aside, haunted)
So were the ravings of this man.
Could he be the Baptist…
or the last prophet?

(BLACKOUT.)

⸻

If you want, I can do the next pass where I:
	•	tighten it to a 12–15 minute Act I opener (festival-ready),
	•	convert the repeated “Set” sections into a chorus refrain that hits every time,
	•	and swap all the real-celebrity references into mythic stand-ins (so you can stage it without legal/tonal baggage).

entries.title: Humans
entries.summary: Excerpt from 'One: The Last Prophet.' Humans fusing with avatars — avatar to avatar, soul to soul, eye to eye. Sci-fi mythic fragment.
entries.body:
Humans…

Excerpt from One: The Last Prophet
(cleaned + tightened, keeping your voice and mythic cadence)

Humans—
exhausted from waking to the same reality each morning—
couldn’t resist the chance to fuse with avatars.

Even though they still could not reach Heaven.

But to stand at the gate—
to breathe the air near eternity—
was enough for them
and enough for their doubles.

Avatar to avatar.
Soul to soul.
Eye to eye.

Thus they made a pact with One:

Everything was going to be alright—
heart to heart,
love to love.

But a cost is always applied.

A cost is applied by the Council
for prowling near Heaven,
for any violation therein,
for entertaining sweet ideas
about One.

And the crows cawed—
in amazement.

////::::::::;;;

The Sanctuary of Dante is the waiting area midway—
where prowlers barter faith against destiny,
and most avatars gather.

Miss the ferry and you will sing,
sing-song praises to Hollywood goddesses and muses,
and send prayers toward Heaven
in the name of One.

Is there a mega-ego in the sky judging everyone—
good or bad, high or low, east or west?

No.

Jesus is a metaphor
for the vision of Christ:
a world where it truly means something
to be human—
to everyone.

It’s that simple.

“Value the work of architects and their designs,”
says the Baptist,
“for they are shaping the future.”

As desert lands turn to oasis—
where you might always bump into One—
furnish your walls with flattering images of him
as if you are expecting his company.

Greet him when you wake,
or when you sleep:
with a kiss, or a slap—

and watch how they do it in Heaven.

“Pretty candid dreams await, in favor of One,”
says the Baptist.

And the Muses sing:

Daughters of Earth—of Earth and avatar—sing.

Athletes and avatars praise working men and women,
for they too are champions—
and they will praise you back.

Working men and women—
Heaven is there for you too.

Heart to heart.
Soul to soul.

⸻

If you want, I can format this as a stage monologue + chorus response (so it can drop into your off-Broadway script cleanly), with the crows as a sound cue and “Sanctuary of Dante” as a set reveal.

entries.title: Prelude to the Trial
entries.summary: Cosmic-mythic invocation addressed to Earth and Heaven. Angels, avatars, and humans mingling for counsel. Performance-ready spoken word.
entries.body:
Pandemic Papers 

Prelude to the Trial

(cleaned + performance-ready)

Brothers and sisters—Earth and Heaven—listen.

In the name of Jesus, Muhammad, and Moses, we address you.

When the Son was given, this mission was placed upon us.

He—the Father of Time—allowed mankind to suffer for a thousand reasons. Yet demons cannot keep long commitments, and angels do not drift far from Heaven. We, however—mortals—were assigned the burden of awareness: to function at a higher level while walking inside ambiguity.

In council with the Trinity, the Almighty reasoned:

Never before had a greater opportunity appeared for angels and avatars to mingle with humans—not for pleasure, but for counsel.

So He summoned the whole human spectrum as witness and jury:

Kings and queens, avatars and muses.
Athletes and entertainers.
Police officers, firefighters, teachers.
Plumbers, ambulance crews, taxi drivers—
and all to whom Earth is of concern.

At last, He turned His attention toward the Adversary and asked:

“Will you ever cease interfering in mankind’s affairs?
Is it not enough that you have the universe to swallow?”

⸻

Heaven and Earth

It will not be long now.

Having released One from tyranny, the Church of Poison and the House of Cards are nearing their final collapse.

Yet those closest to the Almighty complain: strangers bearing gifts—charitable donations—were accepted by the assembly for the first time. Not as bribes. Not as substitutes for tears. Not as prayers disguised as currency.

As a sign of compassion.

For a counsel is considered proper only when its design contains three elements:

Love. Harmony. Prosperity.

And because each contains its own contradiction, none can be conceived without the others—on Earth or in Heaven.

When peace is achieved, war ceases.
When love is attained, hate is subdued.
When harmony is reached, calm is restored—
and prosperity follows.

Remember also the avatars humans created to represent themselves in Heaven, since they could not enter.

Duplicates. Copies of self.
An attempt to be in more than one place at once—
as if mankind could borrow God’s trick without borrowing God’s wisdom.

⸻

To Gabriel’s attention came the silhouette of a beast marked with the sign 666.

No masks.
No hand sanitizer in his toolbox.
No handheld devices. No GPS.

And yet he glowed.

If the one claiming to be Jesus of Nazareth resembles a deity, it is only because of the brightness of his avatar.

When he and the kings and queens of Earth attempted to assault Heaven, they said it was to dispel angst and anxiety.

But this figure who appears in the name of Jesus is no less a fraud for wearing light,
and no less a deceiver for speaking comfort.

Those digital signals they hurled toward Heaven scattered across the universe in every direction, trying to locate what cannot be mapped.

The ones who breached the gates were not men.
They were avatars.

And the avatars—unable to feel pain, unable to hunger, unable to fear—
were left to wander the depths of space for eternity,

like transmissions that never find a receiver.

For if humanity cannot present itself for its own trial before the gates of Heaven, then its case will not be heard.

An avatar cannot bleed.
An avatar cannot tremble.
An avatar cannot argue the point with a soul on the line.

And because Heaven requires consequence for testimony,
humanity’s case has been denied.

entries.summary: A file in The Voice of One canon.
entries.body:
Pandemic Papers

The Coronavirus Notes

By A!Prophet

There were rumors of war. Nobody said what kind.

⸻

Premise

ACT I

Humans on Earth—those who kept a biohazard mask and an oxygen tank near the bed—
were less likely to gamble with their health.

Or so the frightened part of the species believed.

⸻

Case 1

The Supply Run

Shopping for basic supplies—at the neighborhood store—has been elevated to a biohazard nightmare on the street, and it’s not even Halloween.

Fact.

An eighty-nine-year-old launched me ten feet for the last roll of toilet paper.

Fact.

A ninja in aisle four beat me to the last roll of cleaning paper.

Fact.

If shortages persist, the sanitation department may have to make emergency house calls.

Fact. (Or prophecy. You decide.)

⸻

Dispatch

Nation-states were in disarray based on how they handled the event. Infrastructure was not prepared—even in the “advanced” regions: Europe, Asia, North America, Australia.

Fact.

Yesterday, disasters were water, weather, and earth—storms, floods, quakes.
They cost lives, but they felt familiar.

Today’s disaster is microscopic.
A deadly virus.

Pretentious?
You decide.

⸻

Pedantic Square

The Frightened Animal Theory

(Distant music: an old folk song. The kind that makes you remember childhood and regret adulthood.)

No doubt: the frightened animal theory is this—

When danger enters the room, the human becomes what it always was under the costume:
an animal protecting its breath, its food, its family, its fear.

“Who you calling an animal?”

Dear Sir,
Sorry if I offended you. It wasn’t my intention. Please excuse me.

The “animal” I mean isn’t an insult.
It’s a mirror.

It’s Darwin with a pulse.

It’s the survival reflex you pretend you outgrew—
until the shelves are empty.

⸻

Parable

The Virus That Wasn’t Only a Virus

To make a long story short:

Not long after, the world caught a second infection—
not in the lungs, but in the mind.

A kind of code-virus spread through the grid.
Not the kind you can swab.
The kind that makes people run down the street looking for masks and toilet paper like it’s the last sacrament.

It turned crowds into a single organism:
panic with legs.

⸻

Disclaimer

This next part is parable, not instructions.

Some people will always try to turn fear into a “game,”
and turn the world into a puzzle where the winners keep the spoils
and the losers are replaced by machines built for endurance, not tenderness.

That is the sickness beneath the sickness.

A Hunger-of-Systems masquerading as “efficiency.”
A gladiator logic wearing a lab coat.

⸻

The Game

The rules are simple, and ancient:

Those who survive call themselves fit.
Those who don’t are labeled weak—
as if weakness were a moral failure.

Then the winners crown themselves,
and call it progress.

Meanwhile, the shortage of masks and gloves means we import what we lack from far away—
and discover we built a world that cannot breathe without someone else’s factory.

If your connections fail, don’t worry—
most people know someone who knows someone.
And if the broadband goes down, you’ll learn what silence costs.

⸻

Benediction

But in light of today’s event, deepest sentiments go to all in quarantine around the world, and to those who have lost loved ones.

Our planet is in trouble.

And it makes me mad at no one—
including myself—
for loving all of you.

However: when someone stops the narrative—no matter how inconsiderate it seems—
it becomes the responsibility of a Prophet, not an artist.

Please be safe.
And if you can’t be safe, be kind.

entries.body:
Canon Blurb: “Read the Book!”

(cleaned, sharper, publishable — still you)

READ THE BOOK.

This book is built on a dangerous idea:

This is the reign of the Antichrist.

It is a work of fiction—but it circles real questions: power, faith, technology, fear, love, and the hunger for certainty when the world feels unhinged.

At the center is a conflict:

Jesus is on the way.
But not so fast.

Because another figure is already here—
a prophet on Earth, preparing the return of Jesus.

And the question is simple, and terrifying:

Which one is the son of Jesus… and which one is the Antichrist?

⸻
The root of the myth 

Narrator

As a philosopher—not a political scientist, not a preacher—
I’ve made it my responsibility to ask one thing:

Is One truly the son of Jesus?

If he is, I don’t envy him.

Remember what happened the last time someone was called “Savior”?

And if he is not—
if he is the Antichrist, or the one I dare not name—
then the battle for Earth has already begun.

⸻

The Proposition

One’s offer is a peaceful transition.

If world powers agree to relinquish their grip,
One claims he can guide mankind back toward Eden.

But first he must prove to humanity
that he is who he says he is.

And for that—

you’ll have to read the book.

⸻

This story is delivered as an epic poem—sometimes classical, sometimes whimsical, sometimes raw and strange. It refuses to stay in one genre, because the world it describes refuses to stay in one mood.

Regards,
One
